================================================================================
CALLOUT 2: eda.qmd — "EDA in Machine Learning"
================================================================================

CURRENT TEXT (lines 61-69):
  For students of machine learning, EDA serves several purposes:
  
  - **Understanding the data before modeling.** ...
  - **Generating hypotheses.** ...
  - **Diagnosing models.** ...
  - **Communicating findings.** ...

REPLACE WITH:

::: {.callout-note}
## EDA in machine learning

- **Understanding the data before modeling.** What variables are available? What are their types (numeric, categorical, text, date)? How are they distributed? Are there missing values, outliers, or obvious errors? Answers to these questions inform every subsequent modeling decision.

- **Generating hypotheses.** Patterns discovered during exploration become candidates for formal modeling. A scatter plot might suggest a linear relationship; a histogram might reveal a bimodal distribution requiring separate treatment of subgroups.

- **Diagnosing models.** After fitting a model, EDA methods help assess whether the model captures the structure in the data. Residual plots, for example, can reveal systematic patterns that the model has missed.

- **Communicating findings.** Visualizations and summaries developed during exploration often become the basis for communicating results to stakeholders who may not follow the technical details of model fitting.
:::


================================================================================
CALLOUT 3: conditioning.qmd — "Anscombe's Lesson"
================================================================================

CURRENT TEXT (line 499):
  Moral: pay attention to the data! The graphical and tabular summaries we 
  choose to present should be useful and informative. For example, it might 
  be helpful to note that group 2 looks like the partial outline of a 
  parabola. We should note that group 3 consists of 10 points falling on a 
  line, with one outlier. In group 4 we should note that of the 11 data 
  points, 10 have identical $x$-values. We want to minimize the chance of 
  inadvertently conveying false impressions by merely reporting standard 
  summary statistics.

REPLACE WITH:

::: {.callout-warning}
## Anscombe's lesson

Summary statistics can mask dramatically different data structures. Group 2 traces a parabola; group 3 has ten points on a line plus one outlier; group 4 has ten observations at a single $x$-value. Yet all four groups yield identical means, standard deviations, correlations, and regression lines. Always visualize before summarizing.
:::


================================================================================
CALLOUT 4: conditioning.qmd — "Correlation and Independence"
================================================================================

INSERT AFTER line 507 (after "...that is, even if $r = 0$."):

::: {.callout-note}
## Correlation versus independence

- If $X$ and $Y$ are independent, then $r = 0$.
- But $r = 0$ does not imply independence—$X$ and $Y$ can be strongly related yet uncorrelated if the relationship is nonlinear.
- Correlation measures *linear* association only.
:::
